subtopics.name: Astronomical Unit (AU)
content: Definition: Average distance from Earth to the Sun
Value: 1 AU ≈ 150 million km (1.5 x 10^11 m)
Sunlight travel time to Earth ≈ 8.32 minutes
Speed of light = 3 lakh km/s; 1 nm = 10^-9 m #imp

subtopics.name: Light-Year
content: Definition: Distance light travels in one year
Value: 1 Light-Year ≈ 9.46 trillion km (9.46 x 10^12 km)
Used to measure distances to stars and galaxies

subtopics.name: Parsec
content: Definition: Largest practical astronomy distance unit; distance at which 1 AU arc subtends 1 arcsecond angle #imp
Value: 1 parsec ≈ 3.26 light-years
Order of units (smallest to largest): AU < Light-Year < Parsec

subtopics.name: PYQs – Astronomical Units
content: PYQ: Distance between Sun and Earth in light-minutes = 8.311 min (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)

chapters.chapter: Equations of Motion & Types of Motion

subtopics.name: Equations of Motion
content: v = u + at
s = ut + 1/2 at^2
v = final velocity, u = initial velocity, a = acceleration, t = time, s = displacement #imp

subtopics.name: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
content: Uniform Motion: object covers equal distances in equal time intervals at constant velocity and direction
Non-Uniform Motion: object covers unequal distances in equal time intervals; speed/direction changes (acceleration/deceleration) #imp

subtopics.name: PYQs – Motion
content: PYQ: Ball thrown up at 10 m/s, max height with g=9.8 = 5.10 m (Ans: B – SSC CGL)
PYQ: Unequal distances in equal time intervals = Non-uniform motion (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 5s, acceleration = 4 m/s^2 (Ans: B – SSC Phase XIII)

subtopics.name: First Law – Law of Inertia
content: Every object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force #imp
Example: Passengers lean forward when a moving bus suddenly stops

subtopics.name: Second Law – Law of Momentum
content: Rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to applied force; change occurs in direction of force #imp
F = ma; p = mv; a = Δv/t; F = Δp/t
Example: Cricketer moves hands backward while catching a fast ball to reduce force by increasing time (impulse J = F.dt)

subtopics.name: Third Law – Action-Reaction
content: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction #imp
Examples: Gun recoil when firing a bullet; satellite launch vehicle operation; collision of billiard balls (momentum conserved)

subtopics.name: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
content: Balanced Forces: net force = 0; object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity
Unbalanced Forces: net force ≠ 0; produces acceleration, changes speed/direction
Examples: Tug-of-war, kicking a ball

subtopics.name: PYQs – Newton's Laws
content: PYQ: Inertia definition = Tendency to resist change in state of motion (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Statement on rest/uniform motion until external force = First law of motion (Ans: A – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Change in speed or direction signifies = Change in state of motion (Ans: B – SSC CGL)
PYQ: Formula for momentum = p = mv (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)

PYQ: Newton's third law statement = Equal and opposite reaction (Ans: A – SSC CGL)
PYQ: Satellite launch vehicle operation based on = Newton's third law (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Best example of conservation of momentum = Gun recoils when bullet fired (Ans: C – SSC Phase XIII)
PYQ: Correct statement on force = Unbalanced force changes speed/direction (Ans: A – SSC CHSL)

subtopics.name: Archimedes' Principle & Buoyant Force
content: When an object is immersed in fluid, it experiences upward force equal to weight of fluid displaced #imp
Formula: Fb = ρ × V × g (ρ = fluid density, V = submerged volume, g = gravitational acceleration)

subtopics.name: Laws of Floatation
content: Floating: Buoyant Force = Weight; Density of object < Density of fluid
Sinking: Weight > Buoyant Force; Density of object > Density of fluid
Partial submersion: object sinks until displaced fluid weight equals object's total weight

subtopics.name: PYQs – Buoyancy
content: PYQ: Buoyant force magnitude depends on fluid's = Density (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)

subtopics.name: Work
content: Work is done when force causes displacement in its direction
W = F x d cosθ and W = mgh; Unit: Joule (J)

subtopics.name: Energy
content: Energy is the capacity to do work; scalar quantity
Kinetic Energy (KE) = 1/2 mv^2
Potential Energy (PE) = mgh (gravitational); elastic PE stored in stretched/compressed spring #imp

subtopics.name: Power
content: Power is rate of doing work: P = W/t; E = Pt; Unit: Watt (W)

subtopics.name: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
content: Gravitational force is conservative, so total mechanical energy (PE+KE) remains constant #imp
Free fall: at top PE=mgh(max), KE=0; while falling PE decreases, KE increases; just before hitting ground PE→KE(max)
Law of conservation of energy: energy can only convert form, cannot be destroyed

subtopics.name: PYQs – Work, Energy, Power
content: PYQ: 10N force, 2m displacement, work done = 20 J (Ans: D – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: 50kg girl climbs 5m rope in 25s, power = 98 W (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)

PYQ: Quantity conserved under gravitational motion = Angular momentum and mechanical energy (Ans: D – SSC Steno)
PYQ: Law of conservation of energy correct statement = Energy converts form only (Ans: A – SSC CGL)

chapters.chapter: Moment of Inertia and Rotational Motion

subtopics.name: Moment of Inertia
content: I = Σmr^2; sum of products of masses and square of perpendicular distances from rotation axis #imp
SI Unit: kg.m^2; scalar quantity, but value depends on chosen axis
Example: Spinning wheel – determines difficulty in changing rotational speed

subtopics.name: PYQs – Rotational Motion
content: PYQ: Moment of inertia is = Scalar quantity, axis-dependent (Ans: C – SSC CGL)
PYQ: Angular velocity of particle in rigid body about axis = Same for all particles (Ans: B – SSC CGL)

subtopics.name: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
content: Gravitational force between two objects is directly proportional to product of masses and inversely proportional to square of distance #imp
Explains planetary orbits and tides due to Moon and Sun's gravitational pull

subtopics.name: Gravitational Acceleration (g)
content: Definition: Increase in velocity of a freely falling body towards Earth
Average value on Earth = 9.8 m/s^2; formula g = GM/R^2
g depends on Earth's mass and radius, not on object's mass #imp
Variation: max at poles, min at equator; decreases with height/depth; zero at Earth's centre
Galileo's conclusion: in vacuum all objects fall with same acceleration g irrespective of mass

subtopics.name: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
content: Law of Orbits: every planet moves in elliptical orbit with Sun at one focus
Law of Areas: line joining planet and Sun sweeps equal areas in equal time
Law of Periods: T^2 ∝ r^3 (square of time period proportional to cube of average distance from Sun) #imp

subtopics.name: Geostationary Satellite
content: Appears fixed over one point on Earth; used mainly for communication
Height ≈ 35,786 km; orbital period 24 hours; direction West to East #imp
Circular orbit over equator; orbital speed ≈ 3.08 km/s
Uses: TV/radio broadcasting, mobile/internet communication, weather forecasting, navigation

content: PYQ: Importance of universal law of gravitation = Both planetary motion & tides (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Force governing motion of planets, stars, galaxies = Gravitational force (Ans: B – SSC Steno)

PYQ: Geostationary satellites travel at speed ≈ = 3.08 km/s (Ans: D – SSC CHSL)

subtopics.name: Fluid Friction (Drag)
content: Frictional force exerted by fluids on moving objects, also called drag #imp
Acts opposite to direction of motion
Depends on shape and speed, not on contact surface area (unlike solid friction)

subtopics.name: Pressure
content: Pressure = force acting perpendicularly per unit area: P = F/A
SI Unit: Pascal (Pa) = N/m^2; scalar quantity
1 atm pressure = 760 mm Hg
Thrust and Pressure relation: Pressure = Thrust / Area #imp

subtopics.name: PYQs – Fluid Friction and Pressure
content: PYQ: Fluid friction correct statements = Also called drag; depends on relative speed (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Force per unit area on surface called = Pressure (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Area reduced, force same, effect on pressure = Pressure increases (Ans: B – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Formula for pressure = Force/Area (Ans: A – SSC CGL)
PYQ: SI unit of pressure = Pascal (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Relation between thrust and pressure = Pressure = Thrust/Area (Ans: C – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Why we aren't crushed by atmospheric pressure = Internal body pressure balances outside pressure (Ans: D – SSC CHSL)

subtopics.name: PYQs – Sound
content: PYQ: Audible frequency range for human ear = 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (Ans: SSC CGL)

chapters.chapter: Electricity, Heating Effect and Cost Calculation

subtopics.name: Heating Elements
content: Heating element material needs high resistivity and high melting point #imp

subtopics.name: Electricity Cost Calculation
content: Energy consumed (kWh) = Power(kW) × time(hours)
Cost = Energy consumed × rate per unit (kWh)

subtopics.name: PYQs – Electricity
content: PYQ: Crucial property for heating element material = High resistivity (Ans: D – SSC Steno)
PYQ: 2.2kW,220V kettle at ₹4/unit, boiling 30 min cost = ₹4.4 (Ans: D – SSC Steno)

subtopics.name: Magnetic Field Basics
content: Magnetic field lines never intersect; form circular loops around current-carrying wire
Like poles repel, unlike poles attract
Types: bar magnet, horseshoe magnet, electromagnet field patterns

subtopics.name: Fleming's Rules
content: Fleming's Left Hand Rule: relates Motion, Magnetic Field, Current (used for motors) #imp
Fleming's Right Hand Rule: Thumb=Force/Motion, Forefinger=Field, Middle finger=Current (used for generators)
Curl Right Hand Rule: relates direction of current flow and magnetic field around a wire

subtopics.name: Faraday's Laws of Electromagnetic Induction
content: First Law: Changing magnetic flux through a coil induces EMF and current #imp
Second Law: Induced EMF ∝ rate of change of flux; E = -N(ΔΦ/Δt) (negative sign shows Lenz's Law)
Applications: Generators, Transformers, Electric motors, Induction cookers, Microphones, Medical equipment

subtopics.name: PYQs – Magnetism and Induction
content: PYQ: Correctly matched pair on EM devices = Electric bell uses magnetic effect of current (Ans: D – SSC CGL)
PYQ: Transformer works on principle of = Faraday's Law of EM Induction (Ans: B – SSC Phase XIII)
PYQ: EMF induced in rod (length L) moving with velocity v perpendicular to field B = BLv (Ans: B – SSC Steno)
PYQ: Rotating coil generates max induced EMF when = Coil's plane parallel to field lines (Ans: D – SSC Steno)

subtopics.name: Photoelectric Effect
content: Albert Einstein explained the effect using Max Planck's quantum theory #imp
Particle nature of light: light composed of photons (light quanta)
Energy transfer: photon striking metal surface transfers entire energy to an electron
Einstein's photoelectric equation: total photon energy used for work function + kinetic energy of emitted electron

subtopics.name: Life Cycle of a Star (like the Sun)
content: Sequence: Nebula → Protostar → Main Sequence → Red Giant → White Dwarf #imp

subtopics.name: PYQs – Modern Physics
content: PYQ: Correct life cycle sequence of star like Sun = Main Sequence → Red Giant → White Dwarf (Ans: C – SSC Steno)
